subject: Linguistics
title: Language Contact Effects
description: A short lesson to help you apply Language Contact Effects.

hook.text: English borrowed 'they,' 'their,' and 'them' from Old Norse—even pronouns can be imported.

buildup.text: When languages come into sustained contact, they exchange words, sounds, and even grammar.

discovery.text: Structural borrowing is rare but happens—Balkan languages share grammatical features despite being unrelated.

twist.text: The Sprachbund phenomenon shows that geography can make unrelated languages look like relatives.

climax.text: Contact-induced change challenges the family tree model—languages also grow by lateral transfer.

punchline.text: Languages don't just inherit—they also borrow from their neighbors.

quiz.question: What is a Sprachbund?
options: A group of languages sharing features due to contact
